families.title: Controls & tactile inputs
families.summary: Buttons, toggles, pickers and fields with real pressed states and no layout jump.

families.title: Navigation & page chrome
families.summary: Headers, rails, menus and footers that tell people where they are and get out of the way.

families.title: Feedback, status & numbers
families.summary: Counters, progress, loading and messages that stay readable and never shift the layout.

families.title: Overlays & power-user patterns
families.summary: Palettes, menus, popovers and dialogs built on native <dialog>, the Popover API and CSS anchor positioning.

families.title: Data & layout primitives
families.summary: Tables, lists, grids and blocks for showing real data cleanly, with tabular numbers everywhere.

families.title: Motion & CSS craft
families.summary: Curves, transitions and small details that make an interface feel made, all collapsing under reduced motion.

families.title: Sections for pages
families.summary: Whole page sections (heroes, pricing, FAQs, sign-in) built from the same tokens, so a page can be assembled in minutes and still look designed.

families.title: Backdrops & patterns
families.summary: Quiet page backgrounds drawn from the palette: grids, dots, ruled lines, a single-hue wash, pixel dither and circuit traces. One per screen, always behind the text.

ui.name: Grid backdrop
ui.summary: A faint graph-paper grid that fades out towards the edges, with a soft light from the top.
ui.pattern: Decorative ::before / ::after layer (no markup, hidden from assistive tech)

ui.name: Dot grid backdrop
ui.summary: An even field of small dots, like dotted notebook paper.
ui.pattern: Decorative ::before / ::after layer (no markup, hidden from assistive tech)

ui.name: Ruled lines backdrop
ui.summary: Horizontal hairlines at a steady pitch, like a ledger or a notebook.
ui.pattern: Decorative ::before / ::after layer (no markup, hidden from assistive tech)

ui.name: Registration ticks backdrop
ui.summary: Small plus marks at each grid crossing, like a printer’s registration marks.
ui.pattern: Decorative ::before / ::after layer (no markup, hidden from assistive tech)

ui.name: Colour wash backdrop
ui.summary: One hue rising from the bottom of the section, starting below the headline, with a little grain.
ui.pattern: Decorative ::before / ::after layer (no markup, hidden from assistive tech)

ui.name: Spotlight backdrop
ui.summary: A soft pool of accent light from the top centre, low enough in strength to read as lighting.
ui.pattern: Decorative ::before / ::after layer (no markup, hidden from assistive tech)

ui.name: Film grain backdrop
ui.summary: A fine static noise over the section that takes the plastic edge off flat colour.
ui.pattern: Decorative ::before / ::after layer (no markup, hidden from assistive tech)

ui.name: Pixel dither backdrop
ui.summary: An accent-coloured field that breaks into single pixels as it fades out: ordered dithering, drawn to a tiny canvas and scaled up crisp.
ui.pattern: Decorative <canvas> (aria-hidden), redrawn on resize and theme change

ui.name: Circuit traces backdrop
ui.summary: A faint grid with a few accent lines running along it at the sides, a small pulse travelling each one, and a pause button.
ui.pattern: Decorative inline SVG (aria-hidden) + a real pause button

ui.name: Hero, split
ui.summary: Headline, one line of explanation and one primary action on the left; the product on the right.

ui.name: Hero, centred
ui.summary: A centred headline with an announcement pill, two actions and a framed product shot below.

ui.name: Feature grid
ui.summary: Six features in three columns: a quiet icon, a short title and one sentence each.

ui.name: Pricing tiers
ui.summary: Three plans side by side; the middle one is outlined in the accent and is the only filled button.

ui.name: Testimonial grid
ui.summary: Three short customer quotes with a name and role, aligned so the names sit on one line.

ui.name: FAQ section
ui.summary: Heading on the left, questions on the right as native details that open with a rotating plus.

ui.name: Call-to-action band
ui.summary: A calm closing panel with one sentence and one primary action, tinted with a single soft accent glow.

ui.name: Stats band
ui.summary: Four large figures with plain labels, divided by hairlines instead of boxes. Each figure counts up to itself once when the band reaches the screen; the true number is in the HTML.

ui.name: Newsletter signup
ui.summary: One-line email form that validates on submit, explains errors and confirms in place.

ui.name: How it works
ui.summary: Three numbered steps on one thin connecting line, turning vertical on narrow screens.

ui.name: Team grid
ui.summary: Square portraits or initials with a name and role, in a grid that fills any width.

ui.name: Sign-in card
ui.summary: A centred card with SSO buttons, an "or" divider and a passwordless email link.

ui.name: Not found (404)
ui.summary: A calm error page: what happened in plain words, a search box and four ways out.

ui.name: Integrations grid
ui.summary: One linked tile per tool with a two-letter mark, its name and what it is for.

ui.name: Contact section
ui.summary: Ways to reach you on the left, a four-field form on the right that validates on submit.

ui.name: Blog grid
ui.summary: Three latest posts with an image, kind, date and title; the whole card is one link.

ui.name: Feature rows, alternating
ui.summary: Text and a product picture side by side, swapping sides each row, with two ticked details.

ui.name: Logo cloud
ui.summary: One muted line, then six customer logos in an even grid, all in one ink.

ui.name: Article layout
ui.summary: One comfortable reading column with a pull quote, and a sticky "On this page" list beside it.

ui.name: Before and after
ui.summary: One picture in two states with a divider you drag across it. A native range input under the hood: arrow keys, pointer, a tap anywhere and touch all work.
ui.pattern: input type=range over two clipped layers

ui.name: Project grid
ui.summary: A portfolio work grid: large 4:3 plates in two or three columns with the project name, type, place and year.

ui.name: Showcase tabs
ui.summary: A segmented tab row over a framed example; each tab shows a different product with its own palette and type.

ui.name: Customer quote, featured
ui.summary: One quote set as a headline with who said it, and two or three results beside it.

ui.name: Sticky story (pinned scene)
ui.summary: The picture stays pinned while three or four steps scroll past beside it, and it changes with each step: it cross-fades to that step's state, settles in, and the part the step is about is ringed.
aliases: picture that changes as you scroll

ui.name: Offer cards
ui.summary: Two to four things on offer, each with a picture or an art panel, one line, two facts, a price and a link.

ui.name: Visit information
ui.summary: Where a place is, how to get there, how to reach it, and opening hours with today marked and "open now" in words.

ui.name: Hero, statement
ui.summary: A type-led hero: one very large headline across the page, then a ruled row with the pitch, the action and three facts.

ui.name: Hero with video
ui.summary: A headline and one action above a wide picture that is a still first and becomes a muted, looping film when motion is allowed, with a pause button always on it.
ui.pattern: <video muted loop playsinline> over a poster

ui.name: Service list
ui.summary: Things on offer as ruled rows: a name, one sentence, how long it takes and the price, each in its own column down the list. Also a programme with times, or a menu.

ui.name: Scroll statement
ui.summary: One large sentence that lights up word by word as it scrolls past. The keynote beat: a claim set big, with its quieter half in secondary ink.

ui.name: Stack cards
ui.summary: Steps as large cards that pin near the top and stack as you scroll, each with a number, a title, one line and a picture. Replaces a numbered list of paragraphs.

ui.name: Media band
ui.summary: One claim and one large picture on a dark ground, with three facts under it. The cinematic beat of a page; the picture settles into place as it scrolls in.

ui.name: Product reveal
ui.summary: The product rises from lying back, like a lid opening, and settles flat and full size as it reaches the screen. One scroll moment, then three facts.
aliases: product shot that opens on scroll

ui.name: Gallery rail
ui.summary: A row of pictures at one ratio that runs off the right edge and snaps as it scrolls sideways, with previous and next buttons. Many pictures without a wall of cards.

ui.name: Side scroll
ui.summary: A row of work that slides sideways while you scroll down through a tall section, pinned until the last piece arrives. On phones it is a row you swipe, with snap.
states: native swipe (phones, reduced motion, no script)

ui.name: Disclosure chevron

charts.summary: One measure over time, labelled with a clear headline.
charts.bestFor: Continuous change over time for one series
charts.avoidFor: Categories with no order (use a bar chart)
charts.dataShape: x: dates or ordered values; one numeric series

charts.name: Multi-series comparison
charts.summary: Several series on one axis, labelled at their ends, with one highlighted.
charts.bestFor: Comparing 2–6 series over the same time range
charts.avoidFor: More than 6 series (use small multiples)

charts.name: Smooth area chart
charts.summary: One series filled from zero, for volumes and totals.
charts.bestFor: Volumes where the area from zero is meaningful
charts.avoidFor: Series that do not start at zero (use a line)

charts.name: Stacked area chart
charts.summary: Parts of a whole over time, stable layer at the bottom.
charts.bestFor: 2–5 components adding up to a total over time
charts.avoidFor: Comparing individual layers precisely (use multi-line)

charts.name: Vertical bar chart
charts.summary: Ranked or ordered categories with short labels.
charts.bestFor: Comparing up to ~12 categories with short labels, or counts per period
charts.avoidFor: Long labels (use horizontal bar) or many categories

charts.name: Horizontal bar chart
charts.summary: Ranked categories with long labels, read top to bottom.
charts.bestFor: Long category names, rankings, top-N lists
charts.avoidFor: Time series (use a line or column)

charts.name: Grouped bar chart
charts.summary: Two or three series side by side per category.
charts.bestFor: Comparing 2–3 series across a few categories
charts.avoidFor: More than 3 series per group (use small multiples)

charts.name: Stacked bar chart
charts.summary: Totals per category split into parts.
charts.bestFor: Totals plus composition across categories
charts.avoidFor: Comparing middle segments precisely

charts.name: Diverging bar chart
charts.summary: Positive and negative deltas from a zero line, coloured by sign.
charts.bestFor: Changes, variances, sentiment above and below zero
charts.avoidFor: Values that are all positive

charts.name: Lollipop chart
charts.summary: A lighter ranked bar: a stem and a dot.
charts.bestFor: Rankings with many similar values
charts.avoidFor: Small numbers of categories (a bar is clearer)

charts.name: Scatter plot
charts.summary: Two measures per item, drawn on Canvas when there are hundreds of points.
charts.bestFor: Relationship between two numeric measures, outliers
charts.avoidFor: Time series (use a line)

charts.name: Bubble chart
charts.summary: A scatter with size as a third measure and collision-free labels.
charts.bestFor: Three measures per item, up to ~40 items
charts.avoidFor: Precise size comparison (area is hard to judge)

charts.name: Sparkline (line + bar)
charts.summary: Word-sized trend for tables and KPI cards.
charts.bestFor: Inline trends inside tables, lists and KPI tiles
charts.avoidFor: Anything needing axes or exact values

charts.name: Calendar heatmap
charts.summary: A year of daily values as a grid of weeks.
charts.bestFor: Daily activity across months, weekly rhythms
charts.avoidFor: Precise values or short ranges

charts.name: Matrix heatmap
charts.summary: Rows × columns of values, like an hour-by-weekday or region-by-product grid.
charts.bestFor: Two categorical dimensions with one value (hour × weekday, region × product, correlations)
charts.avoidFor: Exact comparison between cells; retention by signup month (use the cohort grid)

charts.name: Candlestick / OHLC chart
charts.summary: Open, high, low and close per period with a volume subplot.
charts.bestFor: Price action for markets and trading products
charts.avoidFor: Non-financial audiences (use a line)
charts.dataShape: bars: t, open, high, low, close, volume

charts.name: Donut chart
charts.summary: Share of a whole for at most four parts, total in the middle.
charts.bestFor: 2–4 parts of one whole
charts.avoidFor: More than 4 slices, or comparing across groups

charts.name: Radial progress gauge
charts.summary: One value against a target on a 240° arc.
charts.bestFor: A single KPI against a goal or limit
charts.avoidFor: Comparing several values

charts.name: Funnel chart
charts.summary: Ordered steps with drop-off between each.
charts.bestFor: Conversion through 3–6 ordered steps
charts.avoidFor: Unordered categories

charts.name: Sankey flow chart
charts.summary: Flows between stages, width proportional to volume.
charts.bestFor: Where volume goes between 2–4 stages
charts.avoidFor: Cyclic flows or more than ~20 links

charts.name: Radar comparison chart
charts.summary: Two or three profiles across 5–8 shared axes.
charts.bestFor: Comparing a few items across the same 5–8 attributes
charts.avoidFor: More than 3 series or precise reading

charts.name: Publication KPI stat card
charts.summary: Big tabular number, semantic delta pill and an embedded sparkline.
charts.bestFor: Headline metrics at the top of dashboards and reports
charts.avoidFor: Several numbers in one card

charts.name: Ranked columns
charts.summary: Sorted columns with the value on top, colour by group and hatched gaps for missing results.
charts.bestFor: Benchmark and leaderboard results across 6–20 entries
charts.avoidFor: Trends over time or more than ~24 entries (use the leaderboard table)
charts.dataShape: items: label + value (null = not available) + group

charts.name: Leaderboard table
charts.summary: Rank, name and group, an inline bar for the main score and heat cells for the rest.
charts.bestFor: Ranking many entries on one score while showing 2–4 supporting metrics
charts.avoidFor: Exact lookup of dozens of columns (use a data table)
charts.dataShape: columns (name, format, better) + rows (label, group, values)

charts.name: Range bars (p5–p95)
charts.summary: A capsule from low to high percentile with a dot at the median, sorted by the median.
charts.bestFor: Latency, price or estimate ranges where spread matters as much as the middle
charts.avoidFor: Single values (use ranked columns)

charts.name: Trade-off quadrant
charts.summary: Labelled scatter with the better-on-both quadrant shaded and median guides.
charts.bestFor: Showing which entries win on two measures at once, like quality against price
charts.avoidFor: More than ~40 labelled points (use a plain scatter)

charts.name: Pareto frontier
charts.summary: A stepped line through the entries nothing else beats on both axes; everything behind it is muted.
charts.bestFor: Picking the efficient options in a two-way trade-off
charts.avoidFor: When one axis does not matter

charts.name: Slope chart
charts.summary: Two columns of values joined by lines, so rises and falls read at a glance.
charts.bestFor: Before/after for 4–12 items where the change is the story
charts.avoidFor: More than two points in time (use a line or bump chart)
charts.dataShape: from, to + items: label + a + b

charts.name: Dumbbell chart
charts.summary: Two dots per row joined by a bar, sorted by the gap between them.
charts.bestFor: Gaps between two measures per item: plan vs actual, men vs women, p50 vs p95
charts.avoidFor: More than two measures per row
charts.dataShape: aName, bName + items: label + a + b

charts.name: Bullet chart
charts.summary: A thin bar against grey bands and a target tick: a gauge that fits in a row.
charts.bestFor: Several KPIs against targets in little space
charts.avoidFor: Showing change over time
charts.dataShape: items: label + value + target + bands [poor, ok, good]

charts.name: Waterfall chart
charts.summary: A start total, the steps that raise or lower it, and the end total.
charts.bestFor: Explaining how one number became another: revenue bridges, budget changes
charts.avoidFor: Unordered parts of a whole (use a stacked bar)
charts.dataShape: items: label + value (+ total: true for subtotals)

charts.name: 100% stacked bar
charts.summary: Horizontal bars that all reach 100%, split into parts with percentages inside.
charts.bestFor: Comparing the mix of 2–5 parts across categories (survey answers, traffic sources)
charts.avoidFor: Comparing totals (the totals are hidden)

charts.name: Histogram
charts.summary: Values grouped into equal bins with no gaps, and a line at the median.
charts.bestFor: The shape of one measure: response times, order sizes, ages
charts.avoidFor: Comparing more than two distributions (use a box plot)

charts.name: Box plot
charts.summary: Median, middle half and whiskers for each group, with outliers as rings.
charts.bestFor: Comparing the spread of 3–10 groups
charts.avoidFor: Audiences new to statistics (use a beeswarm or range bars)

charts.name: Beeswarm
charts.summary: Every value as a dot, packed so none overlap, with a line at each median.
charts.bestFor: Showing individual values and their spread for up to a few hundred points
charts.avoidFor: Thousands of points (use a histogram)

charts.name: Bump chart
charts.summary: Rank over time: lines cross as entries overtake each other.
charts.bestFor: Who led when, for 4–10 entries over a few periods
charts.avoidFor: When the size of the gap matters (ranks hide it)

charts.name: Forecast with range
charts.summary: A measured line that continues as a dashed forecast inside a shaded range, with an optional goal line.
charts.bestFor: Projections, budgets and run-rates where the uncertainty matters as much as the central line
charts.avoidFor: A forecast with no stated range (it reads as a promise)
charts.dataShape: x; values (measured then forecast); from: last measured index; lower / upper bounds

charts.name: Small multiples
charts.summary: One small area chart per series on a shared scale, with the others ghosted behind.
charts.bestFor: Six or more series that would tangle in one line chart
charts.avoidFor: Two or three series (one line chart is clearer)

charts.name: Step chart
charts.summary: Lines that hold flat and jump, for values that are set, not measured continuously.
charts.bestFor: Prices, seats, limits, rates and stock: anything that changes at a moment and then stays
charts.avoidFor: Continuous measures like revenue or traffic (use a line)

charts.name: Annotated line chart
charts.summary: A trend with dashed rules and short notes where something happened.
charts.bestFor: Explaining jumps and dips: releases, incidents, campaigns, price changes
charts.avoidFor: More than about six notes (move them to a table under the chart)

charts.name: Ridgeline
charts.summary: One smoothed distribution per group, stacked with a slight overlap on a shared scale, each with a median tick.
charts.bestFor: Comparing the shape of one measure across 4 to 12 groups: response time by region, order size by plan
charts.avoidFor: Two or three groups (use a box plot or overlaid histograms) or exact values

charts.name: Retention cohorts
charts.summary: A triangle of signup cohorts by months since joining, shaded by the share still active, with sizes and a weighted average row.
charts.bestFor: Retention and churn by signup month or week; repeat purchase by first-order month
charts.avoidFor: One cohort (use a line) or unrelated rows and columns (use a matrix heatmap)
charts.dataShape: cohorts: { label, size, values: % by period }[]

charts.name: Treemap
charts.summary: Nested rectangles sized by value: parts of a whole when there are too many for a bar chart.
charts.bestFor: 10–40 parts of one total, such as spend by team or revenue by product
charts.avoidFor: Comparing similar values precisely (use sorted bars)

charts.name: Gantt chart
charts.summary: Tasks as bars along a calendar, filled by progress, with diamonds for milestones and a today line.
charts.bestFor: Project plans and roadmaps with up to ~20 tasks
charts.avoidFor: Dependencies-heavy planning (use a real planner)
charts.dataShape: tasks: label + start + end (+ done, milestone)

charts.name: Waffle chart
charts.summary: A 10×10 grid of squares with a share filled in, next to the number in large type.
charts.bestFor: One share of a whole that people should feel, like "68 in 100 teams"
charts.avoidFor: More than one or two categories (use a stacked bar)

charts.name: Radial bars
charts.summary: Concentric rings that fill toward a target, with values in a legend beside them.
charts.bestFor: Two to four goals tracked together, like activity rings
charts.avoidFor: Comparing values precisely (rings of different radius mislead; use bars)

blueprints.name: Product / SaaS landing page
blueprints.summary: Top dropdown nav, one focused hero, a live product frame, bento features and a high-contrast footer.
blueprints.anatomy: Navbar → hero (1 primary CTA) → product frame → proof → bento → quote → CTA band → footer

blueprints.name: Financial & analytics dashboard
blueprints.summary: Collapsible sidebar, one global filter bar, a KPI row, a chart grid and a sortable table.
blueprints.anatomy: Sidebar + top bar → title + global filters → KPI row → 2×2 chart grid → table

blueprints.name: Editorial portfolio / showcase
blueprints.summary: Serif + sans typography, generous margins, case-study cards and a comfortable reading measure.
blueprints.anatomy: Quiet header → statement → selected work grid → essay excerpt with pull quote → contact → footer

blueprints.name: Documentation & changelog
blueprints.summary: Sticky left nav, right “On this page” scrollspy, copyable code blocks, callouts and a changelog.
blueprints.anatomy: Top bar → left nav | article | right scrollspy → changelog timeline

blueprints.name: Pricing & comparison page
blueprints.summary: Sliding monthly/annual toggle, three clear tiers, a crisp feature matrix and an FAQ accordion.
blueprints.anatomy: Header → billing toggle → 3 tiers (one featured) → comparison matrix → FAQ → contact line

blueprints.name: Settings & workspace panel
blueprints.summary: Sectioned forms with tactile toggles and a sticky unsaved-changes bar.
blueprints.anatomy: Section nav | form sections (profile, notifications, workspace, danger zone) + sticky save bar

blueprints.name: Interactive directory / skills hub
blueprints.summary: A search bar, filter pills and clean preview cards that filter live, with an honest empty state.
blueprints.anatomy: Title + search → filter pills + sort → result count → card grid → empty state

blueprints.name: Minimal auth & onboarding flow
blueprints.summary: A split sign-in screen, a one-time-code step and a two-question onboarding, with nothing else on the page.
blueprints.anatomy: Quiet brand panel | card: email → OTP → workspace name → done

blueprints.name: Admin list with bulk actions
blueprints.summary: Users table with search, status filter, row selection and bulk actions, a detail drawer, and loading, empty and error states.
blueprints.anatomy: Sidebar | title + count + one action → search + status filter → selectable table → bulk bar → pagination; drawer for detail; ?state=loading|empty|error

blueprints.name: Public status page
blueprints.summary: Overall status, 90-day uptime per service, past incidents with causes and fixes, and email updates; open with ?state=incident.
blueprints.anatomy: Brand + updates link → overall status → uptime per service → past incidents → subscribe → footer

blueprints.name: Changelog
blueprints.summary: Releases newest first with dates, versions and New / Improved / Fixed tags, a filter, and RSS and email subscriptions.
blueprints.anatomy: Top bar → title + subscribe links → tag filter → timeline of releases → older releases → footer

blueprints.name: Store product page
blueprints.summary: Gallery with thumbnails, size and grind choices, one-off or subscription pricing, an add-to-bag button that shows the total, details, reviews, a mobile buy bar and a sold-out state (?state=sold-out).
blueprints.anatomy: Centred shop nav → breadcrumbs → gallery (60%) | buy box (40%) → details accordion → reviews → footer; sticky buy bar on phones

blueprints.name: One-page checkout
blueprints.summary: Contact, address, delivery choice and payment in one column beside a sticky order summary; the Pay button shows the exact total. Open with ?state=error for a declined card.
blueprints.anatomy: Brand + secure note (no navigation) → steps → form (contact, address, delivery cards, payment, Pay £X) | order summary with promo code

blueprints.name: AI assistant chat
blueprints.summary: A history rail (a drawer on phones), a reading-width conversation with prose answers, tables and code, a pinned composer, and empty, streaming and error states.
blueprints.anatomy: History rail | title bar → conversation (max 760px) → Stop while streaming → composer + one-line caveat

blueprints.name: Developer tool landing
blueprints.summary: A floating pill nav over a grid hero with circuit traces, an install command beside the one action, a typed terminal, tabbed code, six plain features, an API teaser, figures, one customer quote and a closing band.
blueprints.anatomy: Pill nav → hero (announcement, headline, action + install command) → quickstart + terminal → SDK code → features → API endpoints → figures → quote → CTA → footer

blueprints.name: Agent workspace
blueprints.summary: A desktop agent app: a workspace switcher and sessions by project in the sidebar, a composer over a dither backdrop to start work, and a running session with a plan, a proposed change and an approval bar.
blueprints.anatomy: Sidebar (switcher → sessions by project → account) | top bar → home: headline, composer, context chips, recent sessions · run: title, plan, diff, approve

blueprints.name: Phone app screen
blueprints.summary: A thumb-first app screen: a large title that collapses on scroll, one headline figure with a week of bars, whole-row lists, a primary action above a bottom tab bar, and a bottom-sheet form. Loading and empty states included.
blueprints.anatomy: App bar (large title) → headline figure + 7-day bars → list: waiting → list: paid → primary action → bottom tabs · sheet: amount, client, terms, send

blueprints.name: Support inbox
blueprints.summary: Views, a conversation list with search and unread state, a thread with a reply box, and a customer details pane. Four panes on a desktop, one at a time on a phone.
blueprints.anatomy: Views | conversation list (search, rows with who, subject, one line, time) | thread (subject, messages, reply or note) | customer (plan, history, tags)

blueprints.name: Calculator
blueprints.summary: A calculator page: labelled money fields and sliders on the left, a live answer with the one action on the right (pinned on phones), a chart that explains the answer, and the questions people ask.
blueprints.anatomy: Top bar → question as the headline → inputs | live result + action → explaining chart → FAQ → footer

blueprints.name: Episode page
blueprints.summary: A podcast or video episode: title and guest, a player that stays in reach, chapters that seek, a transcript at reading width with a progress bar, earlier episodes and an email sign-up.
blueprints.anatomy: Top bar → episode header (number, date, length, title, guest) → sticky player → chapters → transcript → earlier episodes → sign-up → footer

blueprints.name: Place or venue
blueprints.summary: A page for a café, shop, studio, clinic or attraction: what it is and where, the things on offer with prices, a booking bar that answers in a sentence, visiting information with opening hours, and the questions people ask before they come. Art panels stand in until there are photographs.
blueprints.anatomy: Top bar → hero (what and where, book) with a picture or art panel → offers with prices → booking → address, getting here, opening hours → questions → footer

blueprints.name: Local or professional service
blueprints.summary: A page for a practice or a service business (a dentist, a physio, a solicitor, an accountant, a tradesperson): who it is for and where with the first price in the picture, one statement that lights up as it scrolls, fees as tiles with the price set large, the first visit as stacking cards (one holds the written plan), the people as rows, a dark band with whether it is open now, and the questions people ask before they call.
blueprints.anatomy: Top bar with the phone number → hero with the first price set large → scroll statement → fee tiles → first visit as stacking cards → people as rows → find us, open now (dark band) → questions → booking band → footer

blueprints.name: Charity or community group
blueprints.summary: A page for a charity, a food bank, a club or a campaign: the claim in one sentence with three true figures, how to get help with session times, where each pound goes as one bar that adds up, ways to help as tiles with one figure each, the questions people ask, and one giving action.
blueprints.anatomy: Top bar (Donate) → statement hero with three figures → how to get help: where and when → where the money goes → ways to help as tiles → questions → giving band → footer with the charity number

blueprints.name: Maker or product brand
blueprints.summary: A home page for a maker or a small product brand: the object and its price in the first screen, the range as a set at one ratio, how it is made in three steps, materials and care as plain facts, delivery and returns answered, and one buying action. Art panels stand in until there are photographs.
blueprints.anatomy: Top bar → hero (the object, the price, delivery facts) with a picture or art panel → the range as three cards → how it is made → materials and care → delivery and returns → buying band → footer

blueprints.name: Event or conference
blueprints.summary: A page for a conference, a festival, a course or a meetup: the date and place first, what it is in one sentence with three figures, the programme as timed rows, the speakers with their talks, tickets with what each includes, how to get there, and the questions people ask before they buy.
blueprints.anatomy: Top bar (Get a ticket) → statement hero with the date, the place and three figures → programme as timed rows → speakers as ruled rows with their talks → three tickets → venue and doors → questions → footer

typography.name: Editorial Serif + Grotesque Sans
typography.summary: Magazines, portfolios, essays, premium marketing.

typography.name: Precision Dev Sans + Mono
typography.summary: Developer tools, infra dashboards, docs, command palettes.

typography.name: Financial Condensed
typography.summary: Trading, analytics, KPI walls, sports data. Condensed headings fit more numbers per row.

typography.name: Warm Humanist
typography.summary: Consumer apps, health, education, onboarding. Friendly but adult.

typography.name: Swiss Neo-Grotesk
typography.summary: Product marketing, agency sites, posters. Tight, rational, grid-first.

typography.name: Classic Book Serif
typography.summary: Long reads, documentation prose, literary sites. Serif everywhere, generous leading.

typography.name: Geometric Product
typography.summary: Startups, mobile apps, fintech consumer. Round geometry, clean numerals.

typography.name: Technical Mono Display
typography.summary: Changelogs, terminal products, hardware, lab tools. Mono headings, sans body.

typography.name: Luxury Didone + Geometric
typography.summary: Fashion, hospitality, luxury retail. High-contrast display, quiet geometric body.

typography.name: Modern Slab + Sans
typography.summary: Learning products, recipe and outdoor brands, sturdy marketing.

typography.name: Data-Dense Condensed Sans
typography.summary: Admin consoles, tables with 12+ columns, monitoring. Small, sharp, tabular.

typography.name: Friendly Rounded
typography.summary: Kids, games, casual consumer, playful onboarding without going childish.

typography.name: Signage Grotesk
typography.summary: Transport, timetables, stations, routes, maps, parking, logistics and wayfinding.

typography.name: Hyperlegible Care
typography.summary: Health, clinics, pharmacies, care homes, public health notices and accessibility-first services.

typography.name: Stamped Slab
typography.summary: Trades, workshops, coffee roasters, breweries, bakeries, hardware and workwear: goods sold in a stamped bag or crate.

typography.name: Wide Sport Display
typography.summary: Sport, races, fixtures, leagues, festivals, events and tickets.

typography.name: Document Serif
typography.summary: Law firms, contracts, policy, compliance, courts, public records and long formal documents.

typography.name: Workbench Sans + Mono
typography.summary: Developer tools on a light ground: APIs, SDK docs, command-line tools, open-source projects and changelogs.

typography.name: Schoolbook Rounded
typography.summary: Children's learning, schools, reading apps, after-school clubs, libraries and family services.

typography.name: Site Condensed
typography.summary: Construction, civil works, plant hire, site safety, builders' merchants and engineering firms.

styles.name: Studio
styles.summary: Hairline borders, soft surfaces, one accent and almost no shadow. The calm default for products people use all day.
styles.useFor: Dashboards, settings, admin tools, most SaaS products.
styles.notTo: Minimal, which removes the borders and most of the chrome as well.

styles.name: Swiss
styles.summary: Square corners, strong black rules, a tight grid and one signal red. Type does the work, decoration does none.
styles.useFor: Agencies, portfolios, conference sites, editorial product pages.
styles.notTo: Brutalism, which also drops decoration but keeps browser-default parts and ignores the grid.

styles.name: Editorial
styles.summary: Serif display type, thin rules instead of boxes, generous margins. Reads like a well-set magazine.
styles.useFor: Publications, essays, portfolios, research and annual reports.
styles.notTo: Newsprint, which is denser, uses double rules and packs more columns.

styles.name: Neobrutalism
styles.summary: Thick ink outlines, hard offset shadows with zero blur, flat saturated blocks. Buttons physically press down.
aliases: bright blocks with black outlines and hard shadows
styles.useFor: Creator tools, playful consumer apps, launches that want to be remembered.
styles.notTo: Brutalism, which uses raw browser defaults and no colour at all.

styles.name: Terminal
styles.summary: Monospace everywhere, dashed rules, square corners and a phosphor accent on near-black.
styles.useFor: CLIs, developer tools, infra status pages, changelogs.
styles.notTo: Blueprint, which is technical too but uses a drawn grid and blue lines.

styles.name: Glass
styles.summary: Translucent, blurred panels over a soft single-hue glow, with a thin light edge. Calm, not rainbow.
aliases: frosted cards over a soft background
styles.useFor: Media apps, dashboards over imagery, consumer widgets.
styles.notTo: The purple-to-pink gradient hero, which this deliberately avoids.

styles.name: Soft UI
styles.summary: Surfaces share the page colour and lift out of it with paired light and dark shadows. Fields press in.
aliases: soft buttons pushed out of the background
styles.useFor: Calm consumer apps, smart-home and wellness controls.
styles.notTo: Clay, which is puffier, more colourful and uses inner highlights.

styles.name: Clay
styles.summary: Puffy rounded objects with an inner highlight, an inner shade and a soft drop, like modelling clay.
styles.useFor: Kids, habits, games, playful onboarding.
styles.notTo: Soft UI, which stays the page colour and avoids inner highlights.

styles.name: Classic Desktop
styles.summary: Bevelled buttons, inset fields and square windows from 1990s desktop software, kept crisp.
styles.useFor: Nostalgic products, games, utilities, playful internal tools.
styles.notTo: Skeuomorphism, which imitates real materials rather than old software.

styles.name: Blueprint
styles.summary: A faint drawn grid behind everything, dashed construction lines and mono labels. Looks measured.
styles.useFor: Hardware, infrastructure, API references, architecture diagrams.
styles.notTo: Terminal, which has no grid and is all text.

styles.name: Lucid Dark
styles.summary: Near-black panels with a faint top highlight and a 1px inner edge. Dense, quiet and precise.
styles.useFor: Developer tools, issue trackers, pro dashboards.
styles.notTo: Glass, which is translucent and blurred.

styles.name: Flat
styles.summary: Solid fills, no borders on surfaces, no shadows, no gradients. Hierarchy comes from colour blocks.
aliases: everything is just solid colors with no shadows
styles.useFor: Public services, kiosks, simple consumer apps.
styles.notTo: Minimal, which keeps borders thin and uses mostly white space.

styles.name: Minimal
styles.summary: Very few elements, wide spacing, underline fields and text-like buttons. Empty space is the material.
aliases: the page with almost nothing on it
styles.useFor: Luxury, architecture, fashion, single-product sites.
styles.notTo: Flat, which fills areas with solid colour blocks.

styles.name: Paper
styles.summary: A faint paper grain, warm ink and pressed-in labels. Tactile without imitating leather or wood.
styles.useFor: Invitations, journals, stationery, recipe and hospitality sites.
styles.notTo: Skeuomorphism, which copies specific real objects in detail.

styles.name: Elevated
styles.summary: Borderless cards lifted by layered soft shadows, rounded corners and plenty of room.
styles.useFor: Consumer apps, mobile-first products, marketplaces.
styles.notTo: Soft UI, where surfaces share the page colour.

styles.name: Newsprint
styles.summary: Dense serif text, double rules, tight columns and almost no colour. Information first.
styles.useFor: News, data journalism, archives, long dense reference pages.
styles.notTo: Editorial, which is airier and uses single thin rules.

styles.name: Monochrome
styles.summary: Black, white and greys only. The accent becomes ink, so hierarchy comes from weight, size and space.
styles.useFor: Developer tools, documentation, portfolios, anything that should feel quiet and exact.
styles.notTo: Minimal, which keeps a brand colour; monochrome removes it entirely.

styles.name: Graphite
styles.summary: Near-black surfaces, crisp hairlines, small corners and mono labels. No glow, no gradients.
styles.useFor: Developer tools, infrastructure dashboards, trading and monitoring screens.
styles.notTo: Terminal, which goes green-on-black and fully mono; graphite keeps a sans body.

styles.name: Atelier
styles.summary: High-contrast serif headings, wide margins, thin rules and almost no boxes. Feels printed.
styles.useFor: Brands, studios, hospitality, galleries, premium product launches.
styles.notTo: Editorial, which is denser and reads like a magazine; atelier is sparse like a gallery wall.

styles.name: Nordic
styles.summary: Warm greys, rounded shapes, filled surfaces instead of borders and gentle low shadows.
styles.useFor: Health, wellbeing, home and family apps, onboarding flows, consumer tools.
styles.notTo: Soft, which uses pastel tints and puffier shadows; nordic stays grey and restrained.

styles.name: Kraft
styles.summary: Warm paper ground, slab-serif headings, dashed rules and a terracotta accent. Feels hand-made but stays tidy.
styles.useFor: Food and drink, independent shops, studios, newsletters, community sites.
styles.notTo: Retro, which leans on chunky offset shadows and pastel; kraft is quieter and warmer.

styles.name: Midnight
styles.summary: Deep navy surfaces, soft corners and a warm sand accent. Darker and calmer than plain dark mode.
styles.useFor: Finance, wellness at night, media apps, premium consumer products.
styles.notTo: Glass, which blurs and glows; midnight stays solid.

styles.name: Playful
styles.summary: Big rounded corners, chunky buttons that press down, rounded type and a bright accent.
styles.useFor: Education, kids and family, games-adjacent apps, onboarding.
styles.notTo: Neobrutalism, which uses black outlines; playful uses soft colour edges.

styles.name: Enterprise
styles.summary: Dense but calm: grey canvas, white cards with fine borders, compact controls and no decoration.
styles.useFor: Admin consoles, CRMs, HR and finance tools, internal software.
styles.notTo: Studio, which is airier; enterprise packs more onto the screen without crowding it.

styles.name: Zen
styles.summary: Almost nothing: wide margins, light weights, no borders and one muted accent used once.
styles.useFor: Journaling, meditation, reading apps, personal sites.
styles.notTo: Minimal, which keeps borders and normal weights; zen removes both.

styles.name: Tonal
styles.summary: Surfaces tinted with the accent instead of grey, pill buttons, big corners and no borders.
styles.useFor: Mobile-first apps, Android-leaning products, friendly consumer tools.
styles.notTo: Nordic, which uses neutral grey fills; tonal tints everything with the accent.

styles.name: System
styles.summary: Grouped, inset lists on a grey ground, translucent bars, quiet separators and bold large titles.
styles.useFor: Settings screens, mobile web apps, companion apps for native products.
styles.notTo: Enterprise, which is denser and squarer; system follows phone conventions.

styles.name: Noir
styles.summary: Near-black, white serif headlines and no colour at all. Dramatic, quiet and expensive.
styles.useFor: Fashion, film, hospitality, galleries, launch pages for premium products.
styles.notTo: Graphite, which is a working tool UI; noir is for brands and stories.

styles.name: Bauhaus
styles.summary: Geometric type, thick ink rules, square blocks and one red circle as the signature.
styles.useFor: Design studios, architecture, museums, events, bold portfolios.
styles.notTo: Swiss, which relies on grid and grotesk type; bauhaus adds geometric marks.

styles.name: Ticker
styles.summary: Black, amber accents, mono numbers, tight rows and hairline grids. Built for screens full of data.
styles.useFor: Trading, monitoring, operations rooms, analytics power users.
styles.notTo: Terminal, which is green and text-first; ticker is for tables and numbers.

styles.name: Linen
styles.summary: Warm off-white, a bookish serif, an oxblood accent and soft corners. Calm and well-read.
styles.useFor: Publishers, writing tools, education, considered consumer brands.
styles.notTo: Paper, which adds a texture and print shadows; linen stays smooth.

styles.name: Signal
styles.summary: Large tight headlines, a saturated cobalt for every action and square, heavy buttons.
styles.useFor: Developer platforms, fintech, product launches that need to feel decisive.
styles.notTo: Neobrutalism, which uses black outlines and offsets; signal stays clean.

styles.name: Ledger
styles.summary: Ruled rows, tabular figures and navy ink on a warm sand page, like a well-kept account book.
styles.useFor: Accounting, invoicing, banking and any product where people check figures.
styles.notTo: Ticker, which is a dark trading screen; ledger is calm, light and printed.

styles.name: Volt
styles.summary: Near-black surfaces, one lime accent for actions and live states, and crisp geometric type.
styles.useFor: Developer platforms, API products, infrastructure and observability tools.
styles.notTo: Terminal, which is green text on black throughout; volt keeps normal type and saves lime for actions.

styles.name: Civic
styles.summary: Large readable text, underlined links, thick focus outlines and solid, plain buttons.
styles.useFor: Public services, councils, health, education and forms anyone might need to fill in.
styles.notTo: Minimal, which hides affordances for looks; civic makes every link and control obvious.

styles.name: Trace
styles.summary: Near-black pages on a faint grid, one hot accent for actions and traces, and mono labels.
styles.useFor: Monitoring, infrastructure, developer tools and anything that shows live systems.
styles.notTo: Blueprint, which is drafting-paper blue throughout; trace is black with one hot accent.

styles.name: Ember
styles.summary: A dark canvas with one warm wash rising from below the headline, soft corners and a little grain.
styles.useFor: Product launches, tools for makers and brand pages that want warmth without a rainbow.
styles.notTo: Glass, which blurs layers over colour; ember is flat fills with one wash.

styles.name: Pixel
styles.summary: Deep blue-black with a field of single pixels that thins out behind the content, and crisp compact type.
styles.useFor: Desktop apps, agent tools, editors and consoles that want character without noise.
styles.notTo: Terminal, which is mono type everywhere; pixel keeps normal type and puts the texture in the background.

styles.name: Graph
styles.summary: Light graph paper behind heroes, cobalt ink for actions, tight grotesque headlines and square controls.
styles.useFor: Engineering, hardware, data and education products that should feel precise and open.
styles.notTo: Swiss, which is plain white with rules; graph puts measured paper behind the first screen.
